title: Ridley and the museum at night.
lines: Ridley is a six-year-old girl.
She lives in a very special place.
In a museum!
Her mummy is the guard of the big natural history museum.
Every night they look after all the treasures.
And they live there too, in a little flat at the top of the building.
During the day thousands of visitors come.
They look at the dinosaurs, the mummies, the stuffed animals and the old treasures.
But at night, when all the visitors have gone, something magical happens.
Then everything in the museum comes to life!
Ridley is the only one who knows.
She is the keeper of the museum.
Mummy has given her a special key and a backpack with a torch.
Every night Ridley helps her friends.
There's Dudley, a big bison.
He's very strong, but also a bit scared.
There's Fred, a baby dinosaur.
A triceratops, with three little horns.
He's very curious.
And there are three monkeys, Peaches, Leon and Lil Pete, who are always playing tricks.
There's also Ernie, an astronaut who is a bit lost.
And there are the mummies, who love to dance.
One evening Mummy turns off the lights.
The last visitors have gone home.
Ridley puts on her backpack.
She turns on her torch.
And she says the magic words.
The museum is closed, time to play!
And click, click, click.
The animals blink their eyes.
The bison shakes his head.
The dinosaur yawns.
Everything comes to life.
But tonight there's a problem.
Fred, the little dinosaur, is very sad.
He's sitting in a corner and his little horns are drooping.
What's wrong, Fred?
asks Ridley.
I've lost my egg, sobs Fred.
Your egg?
asks Ridley.
The egg I hatched out of, says Fred.
It was always next to me in my display case.
It's my favourite thing.
And now it's gone!
Ridley thinks.
We'll look for it, she says.
I promise.
Ridley, Fred and Dudley go searching.
First they go to the bird hall.
There are hundreds of birds there, on little branches.
Have you seen an egg?
asks Ridley.
We have lots of eggs, says an owl.
But no dinosaur egg.
Then they go to the sea hall.
A big blue whale hangs from the ceiling there.
Have you seen an egg?
No, says the whale in a deep voice.
But the monkeys came past here just now.
They were laughing really loudly.
The monkeys!
says Ridley.
They're always playing tricks.
They find the three monkeys in the space hall.
They're jumping up and down by the rocket.
And what have they got?
A grey, round thing.
They're playing with it as if it were a ball.
They're throwing it to each other.
My egg!
shouts Fred.
Careful!
The monkeys stop.
Is this your egg?
asks Peaches.
We thought it was a ball!
We're sorry, Fred.
The monkeys give the egg back.
Fred holds it carefully in his little paws.
He hugs it.
Thank you, he says.
But then Leon the monkey says: We don't actually have a ball to play with.
That's why we took the egg.
Ridley laughs.
She opens her backpack.
Inside she has a red ball.
You can have this, she says.
But from now on ask first, okay?
They take Fred and his egg back to his display case.
He lies down next to it.
He smiles.
Then the sun begins to rise.
The light falls through the big windows.
Quick, everyone back to your places!
shouts Ridley.
The animals run back.
They stand still.
Click, click, click.
The museum is just a museum again.
Mummy comes to find Ridley.
Was it a busy night?
she asks with a wink.
Ridley yawns.
Very busy, she says.
I had to look for an egg.
And she falls asleep on Mummy's lap.
The end.
